title: Prevent clinically significant norovirus gastroenteritis with a licensed vaccine

concept.text: Prevent moderate or severe norovirus gastroenteritis through vaccination in naturally exposed populations. Clinical development has reached phase 3, but mRNA-1403 did not meet its interim early-success criteria and its next development step remains unresolved. Proposed completion test: FDA or equivalent licensure based on a randomized field trial spanning at least one complete norovirus season, demonstrating efficacy against laboratory-confirmed moderate or severe gastroenteritis with the prespecified confidence interval excluding no benefit. Test set by: Regulators would decide licensure; the mRNA-1403 programme targets protocol-defined moderate or severe disease associated with vaccine-matched genotypes. The season minimum and generic statistical boundary are editorial. Overlaps: VIR-04. Sources given: [NIH January 2026 norovirus overview](https://newsinhealth.nih.gov/2026/01/navigating-norovirus) ; [Moderna November 2026 development update](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1682852/000168285226000194/exhibit9912026q3pressrelea.htm).

page.title: FDA-licensed vaccine against moderate or severe norovirus gastroenteritis
page.definition: An FDA-licensed vaccine reduces the risk of moderate or severe norovirus gastroenteritis, a sudden illness that can cause vomiting and diarrhea, when people in its indicated population encounter the virus naturally. The evidence for protection applies to the age groups and norovirus types covered by the indication.

goal.need: Norovirus causes an estimated 109,000 hospitalizations and 900 deaths each year in the United States. Most deaths occur in people aged 65 or older. Handwashing and safe food and water reduce exposure. Once someone is ill, care chiefly consists of replacing lost fluids. Protection before exposure could spare young children and older adults illness severe enough to need hospital care. The benefit depends on how long protection lasts and which norovirus types are circulating.

completion.title: FDA licenses a vaccine with an indication covering prevention of moderate or severe norovirus gastroenteritis.
completion.criterion: FDA issues a biologics licence for a norovirus vaccine whose approved indication covers prevention of moderate or severe norovirus gastroenteritis in a defined population. The product and manufacturing establishment meet the applicable requirements under 21 CFR 601.2 and 601.4, including evidence of safety, purity and potency. The approved prescribing information defines the population and use.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 601.2(a) and 601.4(a), applied to the proposed norovirus prevention indication.
completion.threshold_quote: that the establishment(s) and the product meet the applicable requirements established in this chapter.
completion.basis: A biologics licence is the regulatory decision permitting marketing of the product for its approved indication. The requirements encompass clinical evidence and manufacturing. This makes licensure a completion test for the stated capability without assigning an unpublished norovirus efficacy percentage or observation-period minimum.

milestones.title: Preclinical and manufacturing evidence permits a norovirus vaccine to enter human testing.
milestones.criterion: An Investigational New Drug application for a norovirus vaccine takes effect, permitting human testing. FDA assesses the preclinical findings, the product’s quality and safety, and the manufacturing technology to determine whether testing in people is reasonably safe.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Vaccine Development – 101; the general vaccine preclinical-to-clinical gate.
milestones.threshold_quote: to determine whether it is reasonably safe for testing of the vaccine to move forward in people.

milestones.title: A phase 1 norovirus vaccine study detects antibody rises of at least fourfold and assesses safety.
milestones.criterion: Assess vaccine safety and detect a rise of at least fourfold from baseline in a participant’s serum concentration of norovirus-specific IgG, measured as an antibody titer. The oral Norwalk virus-like particle study applied this response measure in antibody-positive adults.
milestones.set_by: Baylor College of Medicine investigators, Ball et al. phase 1 study; the fourfold response criterion belongs to this study.
milestones.threshold_quote: responded with >/=4-fold increases in serum IgG titers.

milestones.title: A norovirus vaccine meets a disease-prevention endpoint in a randomised human efficacy study.
milestones.criterion: Meet a protocol-defined gastroenteritis-prevention endpoint in a randomised efficacy study. GI.1 challenge (2011; adults 18–50 years): illness occurred in 14/38 vaccine versus 27/39 placebo recipients (P=0.006). TAK-214 field study (2020; adults 18–49 years): 10/2,355 versus 26/2,357 moderate/severe cases of any genotype over 45 days; efficacy 61.8% (95.01% CI 20.8–81.6). This amended secondary endpoint was met; the vaccine-genotype primary endpoint was not. HIL-214 field study (infants about 5 months): 25/1,425 versus 26/1,399 primary events; efficacy 5% (95% CI −64 to 45), announced 8 July 2024, not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: LigoCyte's NCT00973284 and Takeda's NCT02669121 protocols. The quoted primary endpoint concerns GI.1 challenge in adults; the field study used separate registered endpoints.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary objective was to evaluate the efficacy of the vaccine in preventing the primary end point: viral gastroenteritis caused by the Norwalk virus.

milestones.title: Participants receive a norovirus vaccine in a phase 3 field efficacy study.
milestones.criterion: Begin dosing participants in a phase 3 field trial that evaluates a norovirus vaccine’s safety and efficacy against gastroenteritis under natural exposure.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(c), and the registered adult and pediatric field studies NCT06592794 and NCT06524947.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 3 studies are expanded controlled and uncontrolled trials.

milestones.title: A phase 3 field trial completes its primary norovirus efficacy and safety analyses.
milestones.criterion: Complete the final analysis of the registered primary disease and safety outcomes. In NCT06592794, estimate efficacy in adults aged 18 or older against the first protocol-defined moderate or severe episode due to a vaccine-matched genotype, from day 15 to nine months after the last participant is dosed. In pediatric trial NCT06524947, the primary efficacy outcome includes gastroenteritis due to GI.1, GII.3, GII.4 or GII.17, excluding rotavirus and adenovirus coinfections, during two years of observation starting seven days after full immunization.
milestones.set_by: ModernaTX, NCT06592794, and Anhui Zhifei Longcom Biologic Pharmacy Co., Ltd., NCT06524947, registered primary outcomes. The quoted endpoint is from the adult trial.
milestones.threshold_quote: Vaccine Efficacy (VE) of mRNA-1403 to Prevent First Occurrence of Protocol-defined Moderate or Severe AGE Associated with Vaccine Matched Genotypes

milestones.title: FDA accepts a norovirus vaccine biologics licence application for substantive review.
milestones.criterion: FDA considers a norovirus vaccine biologics licence application filed after receiving all pertinent information and data. The application includes nonclinical and clinical evidence addressing safety, purity and potency, together with the required product and manufacturing information. This is acceptance for review; the subsequent licensing decision is the completion test.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 601.2(a), biologics application filing requirements.
milestones.threshold_quote: shall not be considered as filed until all pertinent information and data have been received by the Food and Drug Administration.

milestones.title: A norovirus vaccine candidate elicits a virus-specific immune response in a laboratory animal.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate a norovirus-specific immune response after immunization in an appropriate animal model. A measurable serum antibody response to the vaccine antigen is one such readout.
milestones.set_by: WHO Expert Committee on Biological Standardization, guidelines on nonclinical evaluation of vaccines, section 3.
milestones.threshold_quote: Immunization studies in animal models should be conducted because they may provide valuable “proof of concept” information to support a clinical development plan.

milestones.title: A randomized phase 2 trial compares immune responses and safety across norovirus vaccine doses.
milestones.criterion: Compare candidate doses or formulations in a randomized trial, measuring immune responses on the protocol’s schedule and recording adverse events. For the HIL-214 infant study, compare four formulations in children aged 6 weeks to 5 months, with antibody measurements on days 1, 56, 84 and 140.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Vaccine Development – 101, phase 2 dose evaluation, as applied in the HIL-214 infant study.
milestones.threshold_quote: examine the relationship between the dose administered and the immune response

milestones.title: Vaccination reduces Norwalk virus gastroenteritis in a placebo-controlled adult challenge study.
milestones.criterion: Show a statistically significant reduction versus placebo in protocol-defined Norwalk virus gastroenteritis after controlled exposure to the vaccine-matched GI.1 strain in adults aged 18–50 years. Compare the frequencies of illness with a two-sided Fisher exact test.
milestones.set_by: LigoCyte Pharmaceuticals, NCT00973284, primary efficacy endpoint.
milestones.threshold_quote: viral gastroenteritis caused by the Norwalk virus.

milestones.title: A phase 2b field trial meets a specified efficacy threshold for moderate or severe norovirus illness.
milestones.criterion: Under natural exposure, show efficacy above zero at the confidence level assigned to the disease endpoint. In NOR-211, count qualifying illness more than 7 days after dosing through day 45, excluding Salmonella, Shigella or Campylobacter coinfection. The GI.1/GII.4 primary endpoint uses a 99.99% interval. The any-genotype secondary endpoint uses 95% if the primary null hypothesis is rejected and 95.01% otherwise. In NOR-212, the lower 95% bound must exceed zero for the first qualifying GI.1- or GII.4-only illness in infants during the primary surveillance period beginning 28 days after dose two.
milestones.set_by: Takeda, amended NOR-211 statistical analysis plan, and HilleVax, NOR-212 protocol, each for its own population and endpoint.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary efficacy objective will be met if the lower bound of the 95% CI for the VE is above 0%.

not_found: No public norovirus-specific FDA or WHO minimum efficacy percentage, confidence bound or full-season requirement was found.
The accessible NCT06592794 record does not supply the severity scoring rules or numerical interim and final efficacy success boundaries.
No published FDA acceptance of a norovirus vaccine biologics licence application was found.

results.finding: In a phase 1 study of 20 antibody-positive adults, every recipient in the highest-dose group had at least a fourfold rise in serum Norwalk-specific IgG titer.
results.detail: The text gives the total study sample but does not state how many participants received the 250 microgram dose.
results.quote: Serum IgG responses to rNV VLPs were dose-dependent, and all vaccinees given 250 microgram of rNV VLPs responded with >/=4-fold increases in serum IgG titers.

results.finding: Among 37 evaluable adult recipients of the intranasal Norwalk VLP vaccine, 49% had at least a fourfold rise in Norwalk-specific serum IgG titer.
results.detail: Table 2 reports the IgG response three weeks after the second dose. The 70% response highlighted in the abstract is for IgA.

results.finding: In 77 adults analyzed per protocol after matched GI.1 challenge, the Norwalk VLP vaccine reduced gastroenteritis incidence by 32 percentage points versus placebo.
results.quote: for an absolute reduction with the vaccine of 32 percentage points (P = 0.006)

results.finding: In the adult rNV-2v phase 1 trial (N=60), the higher-dose arm (n=20) had a 33.8-fold geometric mean rise in serum anti-GI.4 IgG at day 8.
results.detail: Almost all participants had detectable anti-GI.4 and anti-GII.4 IgG at baseline. Table 2 reports vaccine-specific IgG titers in ELISA units per milliliter.

results.finding: Quadrivalent norovirus vaccine trial (n=580, including infants and children) assessed safety and found 93.41% pooled low-dose GII.3 IgG seroconversion.
results.detail: Seroconversion meant a fourfold or greater rise from baseline. The study collected serum from infants and children aged 2–5 years. Children aged 6–17 years contributed safety data only. The pooled rate establishes a pediatric response but cannot show which pediatric age group responded.
results.quote: For GII.3 IgG antibodies, the rates were 93.41%, 92.35% and 18.27%, respectively.

results.finding: Norovirus vaccine phase 2 trial in 420 adults reported zero vaccine-related serious adverse events.
results.detail: Injection-site pain, headache and fatigue were the most common reactions. Antibody responses rose mainly after the first dose.
results.quote: No vaccine-related serious AEs were reported.

results.finding: Among 360 randomized infants, immune responses were similar across all 4 HIL-214 formulations.
results.detail: The trial used descriptive analyses. The safety analysis included 359 infants, and the per-protocol immunogenicity analysis included 306.
results.quote: There were no consistent differences in immune responses between the four HIL-214 formulations.
